answer.rationale: The constraint is severe: 18% cost reduction mandate, 14-day renewal window, zero assembly buffer, and single-decision capacity. Switching primary vendor (memory_c2) carries unacceptable SLA risk given 94% line utilization. Pure renewal leaves the 18% target unmet. Deferring abandons deadline leverage. Adding a second source helps allocation but doesn't solve the cost mandate. Negotiation with incumbent is the only lever that addresses both cost and timeline while preserving operational stability. memory_c4 confirms renegotiation recovers real margin; memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. Verifying c2 and c6 will clarify the SLA confidence boundary and the exact magnitude of pricing available under extended commitment, which determines negotiating room and whether a second-source fallback is necessary post-renewal. This preserves the possibility of a follow-on add_second_source decision in the next cycle if incumbent refuses the 18% reduction.
